items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: The Benchmark Nifty saw a 0.7% rise, signaling a continuation of its positive trajectory. Market analysts foresee a period of consolidation ahead, with a gradual uptick on the horizon. The key resistance levels for the index are 22,650 and 22,800, while support is noted at 22,500. Additionally, foreign portfolio investors recorded net buys of Rs 1,165 crore, contrasting with a trend of domestic outflows.

items.title: Stocks in news: Vedanta, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, HFCL, IREDA, Zen Tech and Oil India
items.description: Indian equities turned around as information technology stocks attracted sustained buying interest. Strong quarterly earnings reports enhanced investor confidence in the market, with the Nifty 50 index achieving a closing point of 23,146, representing a 0.65% rise. Prominent companies like HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank shared their quarterly outcomes, showcasing improved asset quality. Investors are anticipated to keep an eye on upcoming corporate announcements which may guide market trends.

items.title: Nifty rally faces crucial test at key resistance levels: Analysts
items.description: Nifty gained 3% last week, forming a higher-top and higher-bottom structure, indicating bullish sentiment. Analysts suggest it must breach key resistance levels for more substantial gains ahead. Meanwhile, Bank Nifty is approaching significant resistance, which may hinder further upside potential shortly. Key stocks like Coforge, Kotak Bank, and Indian Hotels present buying opportunities based on technical analysis.

items.title: Public sector banks' Rs 7.8 lakh core corporate loan pipeline signals capex revival
items.description: Public sector banks have revealed a corporate loan pipeline of approximately ₹7.8 lakh crore signaling increased credit demand. Companies are stepping up their investment, particularly in sectors like renewable energy and semiconductor manufacturing. Banks report varied corporate credit growth, with some institutions witnessing over 50% increase year-on-year. Mid-sized and large companies are leading the way in capital expenditure, while smaller suppliers are also finding opportunities.

items.title: Banks also count cost of insurance payout curbs
items.description: Central Bank of India anticipates a 33% decline in bancassurance fees due to proposed regulations. Canara Bank expects a ₹145-crore hit to its fee income from similar changes. Axis Bank aims to mitigate losses through increased sales volumes and alternative income sources. HDFC Bank has not yet assessed the potential impact of the new rules.

items.title: Tata Sons reviews AoA to meet Sebi listing norms
items.description: Tata Sons is reviewing its Articles of Association to comply with Sebi listing regulations, which may impact the influence of Tata Trusts on board appointments. This scrutiny follows the RBI's rejection of Tata Sons' application to relinquish its core investment company registration, necessitating compliance with strict governance standards for listed entities.

items.title: Global investors against use of judicial anti-avoidance rule by tax officials
items.description: International investors have raised concerns regarding the Indian Income-tax authorities' invocation of the judicial anti-avoidance rule. At a recent meeting, investors communicated their issues with the Central Board of Direct Taxes on this matter. The use of JAAR to deny relief on grandfathered shares contradicts prior regulations established by the CBDT. The standing of both GAAR and JAAR remains complex due to Supreme Court rulings.

items.title: PC Jeweller shares soar 26% in just two sessions. Here’s what’s triggering the sharp surge
items.description: PC Jeweller shares rallied 26% in two sessions after Cupid promoter Aditya Kumar Halwasiya bought 5.10 crore shares worth Rs 73.60 crore. The jewellery maker recently repaid its dues to 14 consortium banks, achieving debt-free status ahead of schedule.

items.title: Easy exits hurting Indian stocks: Nirmala Sitharaman explains why equities are underperforming
items.description: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman says easy liquidity is allowing investors to exit Indian equities as the Nifty and Sensex struggle to deliver positive returns. Foreign investors have pulled out nearly $63.6 billion since October 2024, erasing nine years of inflows, amid rising US yields, a stronger dollar and AI-driven investment shifts.

items.title: Tech picks: Indian Hotels among 5 stocks to buy for healthy returns in short term
items.description: Indian equities extended their recovery, led by sustained buying in IT stocks, as strong quarterly results and upbeat management commentary reinforced confidence in the sector’s earnings outlook. While rupee appreciation and easing crude prices provide near-term support, analysts say global inflationary and geopolitical risks warrant caution. Sustaining the recovery will require broader earnings growth beyond IT, supported by an improvement in domestic demand and easing margin pressures.

items.title: Kross shares rally 16% after Q2 profit jumps 143% YoY; stock hits 52-week high
items.description: Kross shares surged following strong Q2 FY27 results, with revenue rising 80% and net profit climbing 143% year-on-year. EBITDA more than doubled, while margins improved. Robust commercial vehicle demand, capacity expansion and operational efficiencies supported growth, alongside increased institutional shareholding and the stock reaching a fresh 52-week high.

items.title: Stock Market Holiday 2026: Are NSE, BSE closed on October 20 for Dussehra? Check remaining holidays for the year
items.description: The NSE and BSE will remain closed on October 20 for Dussehra. With 12 of the 16 scheduled stock market holidays for 2026 already passed, three more holidays remain after the October closure. These include Diwali-Balipratipada on November 10, Guru Nanak Jayanti on November 24 and Christmas on December 25.

items.title: Ixigo shares rally 13% after travel platform reports all-time high profit
items.description: Ixigo shares jumped after the travel platform reported a record Q2 profit of Rs 63.42 crore, partly boosted by the sale of its stake in Freshbus. Gross transaction value rose 22% year-on-year to Rs 5,304.47 crore, while revenue grew 13% to Rs 320.96 crore and contribution margin increased 14% to Rs 124.86 crore.

items.title: Balrampur Chini, other sugar stocks slide up to 6% as govt halts diversion to ethanol
items.description: Indian sugar stocks dropped in early trading following the government's directive to cease sugar diversion for ethanol production. The decision impacts major sugar companies like Balrampur Chini Mills and Bajaj Hindusthan Sugar, which experienced a decline between 2% and 6%. This directive aims to enhance domestic sugar availability amidst rising prices. The government's action follows concerns about potential production shortfalls due to insufficient rainfall.

items.title: Bulls retreat as Sensex falls over 400 points, Nifty slips below 23,100. What's next for D-Street?
items.description: The Indian stock market took a hit on Monday after a considerable rise the previous week. Both Sensex and Nifty struggled, with Axis Bank and HDFC Bank suffering significant losses. Nevertheless, firms like SBI and UltraTech Cement managed to post gains. The PSU Bank index rose, providing a stark contrast to the declining private banking sector.

items.title: Yes Bank shares rise as Q2 profit beats estimates, but AT1 bond verdict hit pegged at Rs 5,217 crore. What lies ahead?
items.description: Yes Bank shares rose after falling 17% over two sessions, following a 65% year-on-year jump in Q2 net profit to Rs 1,080 crore. However, the lender cautioned that the reported earnings exclude the potential impact of the Supreme Court’s AT1 bond ruling.

items.title: HDFC Bank shares fall 2% after Q2 results. What are Jefferies, Motilal Oswal analysts saying?
items.description: HDFC Bank shares fell up to 2% after the lender reported a 4.6% year-on-year rise in Q2 FY27 net profit to Rs 19,510 crore. Jefferies, Motilal Oswal, Systematix and Emkay retained positive ratings, citing margin recovery potential and leadership transition.

items.title: Urban Company shares slide 7% as Q2 net loss triples YoY on InstaHelp burn. Should you buy, sell or hold?
items.description: Urban Company shares fell sharply on Monday after its Q2FY27 net loss more than tripled YoY to Rs 182 crore, driven by investments in InstaHelp. Revenue rose 41% year-on-year to Rs 537 crore. Motilal Oswal maintained a Neutral rating but cut its target price to Rs 165, citing profitability concerns and balanced risk-reward.

items.title: ICICI Bank share price target after Q2 results: What are Jefferies, other analysts saying?
items.description: ICICI Bank Share Price: ICICI Bank shares rose after Q2FY27 net profit increased 20.1% year-on-year to Rs 14,843 crore, while net interest income grew 17.7% to Rs 25,339 crore. Jefferies maintained its ‘Buy’ rating with a target price of Rs 1,750, implying 25% upside, citing improving margins and expectations of 16% core profit CAGR over FY26-29.

items.title: 11 years, zero net FII flow: How a $64 billion outflow erased 9 years of equity buying
items.description: Foreign institutional investors have dramatically pulled back from Indian equities, reversing nearly nine years of consistent investment. A massive $63.6 billion in outflows occurred, particularly pronounced in 2026. Industries suffering the most include financial services, automobiles, and oil and gas. Although domestic investors have somewhat mitigated the foreign sell-off, the prospects for renewed foreign investments appear grim, with rising bond yields and energy costs dampening interest.

items.title: Top Nifty50 stocks analysts suggest buying in this volatile week
items.description: Stock Reports Plus, powered by Refinitiv, is a comprehensive report that evaluates five key components of 4,000+ listed stocks – earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum – to generate standardised scores. The simple average of the above-mentioned five component ratings is normally distributed to reach an average score.

items.title: Axis Bank shares fall over 4% despite 38% YoY jump in Q2 net profit. Why brokerages are revising target prices
items.description: Axis Bank reported a 38% year-on-year rise in standalone net profit to Rs 7,003 crore in Q2 FY27, while net interest income rose 12%. Jefferies retained its Buy rating, while Centrum Broking and Dolat Capital lowered their target prices.

items.title: IDBI Bank shares in focus as Q2 net profit falls 39%; NII tanks nearly 50% YoY
items.description: IDBI Bank reported a 39% YoY decline in Q2 FY27 net profit, partly due to a one-off gain in the previous year. Despite this, underlying profitability, margins, asset quality, deposits and advances showed improvement. Meanwhile, Fairfax Financial’s proposed 60.72% stake acquisition marks a major milestone in the bank’s privatisation.
